findings.reason: landing §4 on its declared readiness ships a section naming a verb that does not exist yet, so either the edge or the verb's ownership must move.
findings.text: §4 says priority "changes while queued with `crew queue reprioritise`", but §5 is the section that adds that verb ("Add `crew queue list | show | edit | reprioritise | drop`" — snapshot line 63), and `plan-section-depends-on` carries no `s4→s5` edge, so §4's own text uses a command no landed section provides

findings.reason: the picker would read a priority nothing sets, and the followup's claim that "§5 and §7 can run beside it" is what let this edge go unconsidered.
findings.text: §7's mechanism reads a request's `priority` ("requests at or above a stated priority and capability") and defers ordering to "§4's ranking", but §7 declares no dependency on §4, so §7 can launch before the field it reads is defined

findings.reason: a node reading "kept" may preserve an exemption attached to nothing or delete it outright, regressing the landed plan; the section must state that the exemption now attaches to the project bound.
findings.text: §3 retires "the 2–8 per-session clamp" and in the same section says "The review exemption from a-coordinator-can-clear-its-own-duties is kept", but in that cited plan the exemption exists only as an exemption from the per-session queue cap (its §2: "Reviews are exempt from the per-session queue cap"); with the cap gone the exemption has no referent, while §4 separately carries review precedence ("Reviews of delivered runs keep their precedence")

findings.reason: the plan's own real-code-path check fails as written, and a node may implement a landing routine nothing calls without the plan contradicting it.
findings.text: §6 asserts a delivered run "lands mechanically" but names no process that performs the landing: §2 names the driver for its own mechanism ("Each admission pass re-reads readiness"), and §6 names none for either the landing or the wake conditions, so the mechanism is specified with no production caller

findings.reason: the repository already pins a starvation age in `reckon/crew/queue_order.py`, so an implementer will reuse it and the assertion stays falsifiable; naming the constant would tighten the section but not redirect a node.
findings.text: §4's done-when asserts "A lowest-priority request launches within the ageing bound" and the prose says ageing makes it launch "within a stated bound", but no bound is stated anywhere in the plan, so the implementer supplies the number the assertion is then measured against

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — all four cited plan hrefs resolve to existing files under `docs/plans/` (`a-held-dispatch-waits-its-fair-turn.html`, `a-coordinator-can-clear-its-own-duties.html`, `crew-state-stays-bounded.html`, `a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk.html`), and each cited code anchor resolves: `QUEUED_DISPATCH_CAP_FLOOR`/`QUEUED_DISPATCH_CAP_CEILING` at `reckon/crew/runs.py:367-368`, `reckon/crew/queue_order.py`, the earlier-overlapping-request hold at `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:467`, and `admission.sessions`/`fair_share` at `reckon/crew/lane_document.py:121,127`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §4's third assertion measures against an "ageing bound" the section never states (snapshot line 59).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — no node names a session scratchpad, node-local temporary directory or other non-durable path; the done-whens are test measures and the only path-like delegation (§3's read-time budget) points at the `crew-state-stays-bounded` plan rather than a temp location.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol; section numbers appear only in plan prose, and no comment or docstring the plan proposes would carry one.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — two mechanisms do not run on the real code path: §3 retains a review exemption from the cap it retires, and §6's mechanical landing names no process that performs the landing.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of §2–§7 names one deliverable (wait-on-dependency admission, depth bound, admission ranking, launch-time brief binding, mechanical landing, lift preference); the secondary mechanisms in §3 and §4 are parts of their section's single goal, not separate deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §4 depends on the `crew queue reprioritise` verb that §5 is the section which adds, and neither section declares that edge; §7 likewise rests on §4's `priority` (snapshot line 57).
